stories.title: Invesco Reports Stronger Earnings in Q2 With 20% Revenue Jump
stories.excerpt: Investment management firm Invesco reported better-than-expected earnings results for the second quarter of 2026. During the second quarter, Invesco posted adjusted income of $322.3 million, or 71 cents per share, comfortably above the Zacks Consensus estimate of 67 cents per share. Adjusted net revenue for the quarter that ended June 30, 2026, came in at $1.83 billion, a more than 20 percent increase from $1.52 billion during the same period last year. “We have built significant momentum thus far in 2026 as we continue to execute against our strategic priorities,” Invesco CEO Andrew Schlossberg said Tuesday during Invesco’s earnings call. “Our broad product suite and global reach is resonating with clients as they seek to navigate an ever more complex market environment.” The firm also reported $2.5 trillion in ending assets under management (AUM) during the second quarter, which represents an increase of 14.4 percent from the second quarter of 2025. Invesco also reported that its QQQ fund, the firm’s privately managed, exchange-traded fund (ETF), brought in $13.8 billion of net inflows. “In the first half of 2026, the Qs’ AUM grew 20 percent and it produced strong organic net flow growth in the second quarter,” Schlossberg said. “We have significant opportunities to continue to expand this flagship, competitively advantaged product, not only here in the United States, where the traction is incredibly strong, but also in other international markets.” The QQQ fund is now cross-listed on both the Hong Kong and Tokyo stock exchanges, and has raised $10 billion of AUM there so far. “We see several avenues to continue to expand QQQ’s client base, our innovation suite in general, and our wider $1.25 trillion ETF complex,” Schlossberg continued. bullets: Invesco Q2 2026: $1.83B revenue (+20% YoY), $2.5T AUM (+14.4% YoY)
Strong institutional capital flows into investment products amid market complexity
Asset manager health signals continued investor appetite for diversified real estate funds
stories.summary: Invesco reported Q2 2026 adjusted net revenue of $1.83 billion, up more than 20% from $1.52 billion in Q2 2025, with assets under management climbing 14.4% to $2.5 trillion. The firm's CEO cited broad product suite and global reach resonating with clients navigating complex markets. Adjusted earnings of 71 cents per share beat consensus estimates.
stories.impact: Healthy asset manager earnings and growing AUM indicate robust institutional capital available for real estate fund commitments. This supports multifamily development financing pipelines through REIT and commingled fund vehicles, though the article provides no specific sector or geographic signals.

stories.title: JV Lands $202M Construction Financing for Naples Mixed-Use Venture
stories.excerpt: APREA and JSB Capital Group closed on a $202 million construction financing package with Bayview Commercial Mortgage Finance (BCMF) on The Avenue. The funding includes includes $109 million of C-PACE financing and a $93 million traditional construction loan. The milestone kickstarts construction of the mixed-use development near downtown Naples. The Avenue will include for-sale residences and retail options. Bayview PACE, a division of BCMF, is providing $109 million in Commercial Property-Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing across two assessments and closings, in a deal brokered by JLL’s Debt Advisory team, led by Scott Aiese and Alex Staikos.  The Avenue will introduce 75,000 square feet of boutique retail, dining, wellness, and lifestyle offerings beneath a limited collection of 50 luxury residences. Construction is being led by DeAngelis Diamond. Move-ins anticipated in early 2028. The post JV Lands $202M Construction Financing for Naples Mixed-Use Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: APREA/JSB closed $202M construction financing on The Avenue, Naples: $109M C-PACE + $93M traditional
Bayview Commercial Mortgage Finance led PACE underwriting; 50 luxury residences + 75K SF retail
Move-in timeline: early 2028; mixed-use urban infill near downtown Naples
stories.summary: A joint venture of APREA and JSB Capital Group secured $202 million in construction financing for The Avenue in downtown Naples, comprising $109 million in C-PACE financing and $93 million in traditional construction debt from Bayview Commercial Mortgage Finance. The mixed-use project will deliver 50 luxury for-sale residences and 75,000 square feet of retail, dining, wellness, and lifestyle space, with move-ins expected in early 2028. DeAngelis Diamond is the construction partner.
stories.impact: C-PACE as primary funding source (54% of deal) signals continued reliance on energy-efficiency financing to underwrite mixed-use projects in the absence of aggressive traditional construction lending. The for-sale residential component limits relevance to rental multifamily, but demonstrates strong capital appetite for quality mixed-use in South Florida submarkets.

stories.title: Developer Duo Eyeing $100M Investment in Greensboro Mixed-Use Venture
stories.excerpt: Simpson Commercial Real Estate and Brown Investment Properties purchased 61.7 acres near Toyota’s $14 billion battery manufacturing facility (shown), with plans to develop a mixed-use project to be called Woody Mill. The joint venture paid $8 million for the site. The Triad Business Journal reports the team is planning to build a 240-unit Class A multifamily project, along with seven outparcels that will be retail-oriented, featuring restaurants and office space. The apartments would cost roughly $50 million, the commercial sector would cost roughly $30 million and the outparcels would cost roughly $20 million. The developers, who started the project a year and a half ago, will decide on more concrete plans for Woody Mill by September and plan to break ground before the year ends. They plan for the development to be open in the first or second quarter of 2028. The post Developer Duo Eyeing $100M Investment in Greensboro Mixed-Use Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Simpson Commercial RE & Brown Investment Properties: 61.7-acre Greensboro site near Toyota $14B battery plant, $8M acquisition
Woody Mill mixed-use: 240-unit Class A multifamily ($50M), retail/office outparcels ($50M total), $100M venture
Ground break targeted year-end 2026; delivery Q1–Q2 2028; finalized plans due September 2026
stories.summary: Simpson Commercial Real Estate and Brown Investment Properties purchased 61.7 acres near Toyota's $14 billion battery manufacturing facility in Greensboro for $8 million, planning a $100 million mixed-use development called Woody Mill. The project includes 240 Class A multifamily units budgeted at $50 million, seven retail-oriented outparcels (restaurants, office) at $30 million, and additional commercial components at $20 million. Developers plan finalized designs by September and ground break before year-end 2026, with opening targeted for Q1–Q2 2028.
stories.impact: Toyota's battery plant is a major employer catalyst for Greensboro; this acquisition signals developer confidence in job creation and population inflow to the market over the next 18–24 months. The 240-unit multifamily pipeline ahead of plant ramp-up positions Woody Mill to capture early demand from new workers and management relocations. Greensboro will see supply influx in 2028; early-mover advantage and proximity to the plant are key lease-up drivers.

stories.title: Cynde Altheim Interiors Renews 7K SF at 149 West 36th Street
stories.excerpt: Interior design firm Cynde Altheim Interiors is holding onto its third-floor lease at 149 West 36th Street. Cynde Altheim will maintain its 6,740-square-foot office space in the Frangene Company-owned building, located between Broadway and Seventh Avenue. The design firm, which operates under the name of Mark David Interiors, specializes in residential and commercial projects. Cynde Altheim arrived at the Garment District address in 2014. Its six-year renewal was one of two recent deals arranged directly with tenants by Lee & Associates NYC’s Noah Caspi and Todd Korren, who represented the landlord. The second renewal belonged to Excel Graphics, a full-service printing and graphics company, which moved to its fifth-floor office space at 149 West 36th Street in 2019. The company signed an eight-year renewal for its 4,500-square-foot space. “Both tenants carefully evaluated their options before committing to long-term renewals and ultimately recognized the advantages of remaining at the building,” Korren said in a statement. “Retaining quality tenants through direct negotiations is a win for both ownership and the occupants in any market.” The brokers did not disclose asking rents for the two deals, but asking rents for Class B office space in Midtown South averaged $81.14 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield data. The 12-story, 58,000-square-foot office building is managed on behalf of the landlord by GFP Real Estate. Additional tenants there include the United Parcel Service, which inked a deal on the ground floor of the adjoining building at 147 West 36th Street in April, as well as textile importer Liba Fabrics. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Cynde Altheim Interiors renewed 6,740 SF office, third floor, 149 West 36th Street Manhattan (6-year term)
Excel Graphics also renewed 4,500 SF fifth floor (8-year term); Garment District building
Both tenants re-evaluated alternatives; chose to remain at location
stories.summary: Interior design firm Cynde Altheim Interiors renewed its 6,740-square-foot office lease on the third floor of 149 West 36th Street in Manhattan's Garment District for six years, while print and graphics company Excel Graphics signed an eight-year renewal for 4,500 square feet on the fifth floor. Both tenants conducted market evaluations before committing to renewals. Lee & Associates NYC brokered both transactions. The building is owned by Frangene Company.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office lease activity in Manhattan's Garment District reflects tenant confidence in workspace retention rather than market-moving demand signals; no implication for residential supply, demand, or capital.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges Sale, Financing for Charlotte Affordable Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Ascent Housing paid $28.8 million for a 140-unit affordable multifamily community in Charlotte. To help fund the deal, the company closed on $15.9 million in acquisition financing. Eller Capital was the seller of the Reserve at Waterford Lakes at 8725 Kody Marie Court. Newmark arranged the sale and acquisition financing. Newmark’s Jason Kon, Dean Smith, John Heimburger, Sean Wood, John Munroe and Brenna Campbell represented the seller. Josh Davis and Patrick Breed secured the financing through Freddie Mac. Ascent Housing is committed to maintaining affordability while investing in resident-focused programming, including on-site collaborations that support financial empowerment, education, health and wellness initiatives. Built in 2008, Reserve at Waterford Lakes offers one- and two-bedroom apartment homes featuring modern kitchens with black or stainless steel appliances, glass cooktops, nine-foot ceilings and crown molding. Community amenities include a swimming pool, fitness center, resident lounge with games, business center and outdoor picnic and grilling areas.  The post Newmark Arranges Sale, Financing for Charlotte Affordable Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ascent Housing acquired Reserve at Waterford Lakes, Charlotte: 140-unit affordable, $28.8M purchase price
Freddie Mac provided $15.9M acquisition financing (55% LTV); Josh Davis and Patrick Breed structured deal
Built 2008, 1–2 BR units; Ascent committed to affordability + resident programming
stories.summary: Ascent Housing purchased the Reserve at Waterford Lakes, a 140-unit affordable multifamily community in Charlotte, for $28.8 million, closing $15.9 million in acquisition financing through Freddie Mac arranged by Newmark. The property, built in 2008, features one- and two-bedroom units and community amenities including pool and fitness center. Ascent has pledged to maintain affordability while funding resident-focused health, wellness, and financial empowerment programs.
stories.impact: Freddie Mac's willingness to finance affordable rentals at ~55% LTV in Charlotte indicates sustained agency appetite for preserving workforce housing stock. Ascent's acquisition signals investor confidence in Charlotte's affordable market; low purchase basis and secondary-market pricing suggest limited new supply competition. No direct impact on market-rate development fundamentals.

stories.title: Can Nithya Raman Make L.A. a City of Yes?
stories.excerpt: In the race for mayor of Los Angeles, housing — and the subsequent problems of affordability, homelessness, economic opportunity and safety that are so closely intertwined — remains the issue of the day. Progressive Councilmember Nithya Raman, who narrowly edged out realty TV personality Spencer Pratt to clinch a spot in the November runoff election, sees the crisis as one of the city’s own doing, and one that can be mollified with smarter policy that provides developers with certainty, speed, and more places to build. Los Angeles City Councilmember and mayoral candidate Nithya Raman speaks to the media. PHOTO: Mario Tama/Getty Images “She sees there’re no silver bullets,” said Scott Epstein, director of policy at Abundant Housing L.A. “I don’t think anybody should have the illusions that in the first year of the Nithya Raman administration, that everything is going to turn around and all of a sudden we’re going to have gangbusters housing production pipeline. But I think when you look at the totality of what she is proposing, it is really changing the culture around housing production in the city. It’s saying we’re going to be a city of yes.” It’s a YIMBY-friendly approach that befits Raman’s technocratic nature. She’s an MIT-educated urban planner by training, and current head of the City Council’s Housing and Homelessness Committee who has long been in the weeds in the city’s housing debates. If elected mayor, her ability to issue executive orders and shake up city agencies could be a promising start to a mayoralty built on housing reform. “Building in any city in California, especially Los Angeles, is complex,” said David Garcia, deputy director of policy for the University of California Berkeley’s Terner Center for Housing Innovation. “A lot of the solutions are to create certainty through simplification of the process. bullets: L.A. mayoral runoff: progressive Councilmember Nithya Raman proposes policy certainty and speed for developers
Raman's platform: zoning reform, streamline approvals, expand buildable land to ease affordability crisis
Policy shift aims to change housing production culture; realistic timeline beyond first-year administration
stories.summary: Los Angeles City Councilmember Nithya Raman, a progressive mayoral candidate who advanced to the November runoff, is campaigning on housing-centric policy emphasizing developer certainty, faster approvals, and expanded land for development. Her platform targets zoning reform and regulatory streamlining to unlock supply and address the city's affordability crisis. Policy experts note that meaningful production gains will take multiple years, though her proposals represent a fundamental shift in the city's approach to housing approval culture.
stories.impact: If elected, Raman's administration could materially accelerate entitlement timelines and reduce discretionary review burden for infill and mixed-use projects across Los Angeles submarkets, directly lowering development risk and improving underwriting IRRs. Zoning expansion could unlock constrained sites in core markets (Silver Lake, Highland Park, Koreatown). Current regulatory uncertainty depresses L.A. development economics; policy shift toward density would improve feasibility for Class A multifamily in primary and secondary infill markets.

stories.title: High-Growth Retail Brands Expand with Data-Driven Site Selection
stories.excerpt: Across segments, retail and dining expansions converge on a common set of priorities, Placer.ai says in a new white paper. These include identifying markets with strong demand, ensuring alignment with target audiences and leveraging local consumer behavior to drive synergy.  Titled What High-Growth Brands Know About Picking the Right Location, the white paper delves into key signals guiding data-driven site selection from brands actively expanding their brick-and-mortar footprints. Key insights include the following: Targeting Regions With Durable Demand: Evaluating both total and per-location demand helps distinguish true expansion opportunities from saturated markets. Ensuring Hyperlocal Demographic Alignment: Aligning site-level visitor profiles with a brand’s core customer base can drive stronger performance and reinforce positioning. Matching Locations to Complementary Visitation Patterns: Selecting sites where traffic patterns support a brand’s operating model improves both fit and long-term success. Leveraging Proximity to Competitors and Complementary Brands: Co-tenancy can act as a demand driver by capturing shared traffic and strengthening destination appeal.‍ Assessing Trade Area Overlap to Mitigate Cannibalization Risk: Analyzing trade areas ensures new locations generate incremental demand rather than redistribute existing visits. The post High-Growth Retail Brands Expand with Data-Driven Site Selection appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Placer.ai white paper: high-growth retail/dining brands use data-driven site selection and local consumer behavior
Priorities: strong demand identification, target audience alignment, synergy with existing consumer patterns
No specific market or brand expansion data provided
stories.summary: Placer.ai published a white paper on site selection strategy for high-growth retail and dining brands, highlighting data-driven priorities including demand identification, target audience alignment, and consumer behavior alignment. The analysis draws insights from brands actively expanding their brick-and-mortar footprints across segments.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Retail tenant site selection behavior is a secondary signal for mixed-use and transit-oriented multifamily (co-tenancy and foot-traffic benefit), but this article provides no specific market, submarket, or demographic data applicable to residential underwriting.

stories.title: Citizens Bank Refis N.J. Industrial Property With $47M Loan
stories.excerpt: Wholesale product company EXP Group has landed $47 million of permanent debt to refinance an industrial asset in northern New Jersey, Commercial Observer has learned. Citizens Bank provided the loan on the 300,015-square-foot logistics property at 2500 83rd Street in North Bergen, N.J. Ripco Real Estate arranged the transaction with a team consisting of Adam Hakim, Michael Winter and James Murad. “Despite a challenging lending environment, high-quality industrial assets with strong sponsorship continue to attract lender interest,” Murad, managing director at Ripco, said in a statement. Situated on 35 acres, 2500 83rd Street features a single-story, 100 percent-occupied industrial facility that served as EXP Group’s Northeast headquarters and distribution hub along with other industrial tenants. The property benefits from being in a supply-constrained industrial market with access to major transportation corridors and ports, according to Ripco. EXP Group and Citizens Bank did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: EXP Group refinanced 300K SF industrial property, North Bergen, N.J.: $47M Citizens Bank loan, 35-acre site
100% occupied, single-tenant + other industrial users; Northeast HQ and distribution hub
Supply-constrained market with access to major transportation corridors and ports
stories.summary: Wholesale products company EXP Group closed a $47 million permanent refinancing loan from Citizens Bank on a 300,015-square-foot industrial property at 2500 83rd Street in North Bergen, New Jersey. The 35-acre site is fully occupied and serves as EXP Group's Northeast headquarters and distribution hub alongside other industrial tenants. The property benefits from proximity to major transportation corridors and ports in a supply-constrained market.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Industrial financing activity and supply constraints in northern New Jersey do not signal direct demand drivers for residential; logistics concentration near ports may indicate blue-collar wage and employment growth, a secondary demand tailwind for workforce housing, but this story provides insufficient data.

stories.title: Welltower Reports Revenue and Income Growth From Senior Housing Investments
stories.excerpt: Welltower, an investment firm focused on senior and assisted living communities, reported continued balance sheet improvement in the second quarter of 2026. In a Tuesday earnings call, the real estate investment trust (REIT) announced a slew of acquisitions, such as the Amica Senior Lifestyles portfolio consisting of 38 communities for $1.91 billion, as well as the disposition of $7.2 billion in outpatient medical properties. On July 2, Welltower also closed on a deal to acquire five properties currently under development in Canada for about $459 million. Completion of those properties is expected in 2027. Overall, the Ohio-based firm invested $9.5 billion in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. since the beginning of the year, Shankh Mitra, CEO of Welltower, said during the earnings call. “As the Welltower business system continues to mature, our ability to increase cash flow following an acquisition has become both more significant and more repeatable,” Mitra said. “That distinction matters. Spread investing and cost of capital arbitrage are not value creation, nor are they durable investment strategies. Our focus is different. We seek to acquire assets at a fair price, based on a reasonable view of their prospective cash flows while retaining for our owners the upside we believe our platform can create beyond that.” Funds from operations (FFO) in the second quarter reached $1.60 per share compared to $1.28 per share from the same period last year, while revenue for the quarter was $3.54 billion, an increase from the $2.55 billion recorded on a year-over-year basis. Net income was $12.2 billion, compared to $10.6 billion in the second quarter of 2025. Welltower also saw a 5.2 percent growth in revenue per occupied room, with the average number of occupied rooms in its portfolio at 100,410 compared to 96,800 on a year-over-year basis. bullets: Welltower Q2 2026: $9.5B invested YTD in senior/assisted living; $1.91B Amica portfolio (38 communities) acquired
Disposition of $7.2B outpatient medical properties; five Canadian properties under development, ~$459M, completion 2027
Senior housing portfolio expansion and medical real estate redeployment signal capital reallocation
stories.summary: Welltower, a senior and assisted living-focused REIT, reported $9.5 billion in year-to-date investments across the U.S., Canada, and U.K., including the $1.91 billion acquisition of the 38-community Amica Senior Lifestyles portfolio. The firm also divested $7.2 billion in outpatient medical properties and closed a $459 million deal for five Canadian properties under development, due to complete in 2027. CEO Shankh Mitra emphasized the maturation of Welltower's acquisition integration model and spread-based capital deployment.
stories.impact: Welltower's massive senior housing expansion and medical property exit signal capital migration toward aging demographics and away from office-adjacent medical. This does not directly compete with multifamily; however, large senior housing pipeline growth in markets like Florida, Arizona, and California could increase land scarcity and construction labor competition in core multifamily markets.

stories.title: North American Office Posts Strongest Performance Since Pandemic
stories.excerpt: The North American office market is having its best year since the COVID-19 lockdown upended demand for the sector, with vacancy declines in the second quarter across Canada and the United States for the first time since 2019, Lee & Associates reported. “Tenant growth has returned and institutional investors are showing greater confidence in premium assets,” the firm said in its 2026 Q2 North American Market Report. “Also, with little new space being built and more obsolete office properties being redeveloped, total inventories in the U.S. and Canada declined together for the first time on record.” The turnaround for U.S. office over the past four quarters has totaled 29.7 million square feet. Following first-half net growth of 16.7 million square feet, the U.S. market is on track in 2026 to halt its six-year slide in tenant expansion. Year-to-date net absorption in Canada totals 4.4 million square feet and this year could surpass the 5.4-million-square-foot total for 2019. Not all metros report strong performances, though. New York City, Dallas, Austin, Houston, San Francisco and San Jose are surging, while Los Angeles, Chicago, St. Louis and Washington, D.C., still seek stability, reported Lee & Associates. The post North American Office Posts Strongest Performance Since Pandemic appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: U.S. office posted first Q2 vacancy decline since 2019; 29.7M SF net absorption over 4 quarters
Canada: 4.4M SF YTD absorption, tracking above 5.4M SF 2019 baseline; inventory declining for first time on record
Strong metros (NYC, Dallas, Austin, Houston, SF, San Jose); weak metros (L.A., Chicago, St. Louis, D.C.) still stabilizing
stories.summary: The North American office market recorded its strongest performance since the pandemic, with the second quarter marking the first vacancy decline in both the U.S. and Canada since 2019. The U.S. has absorbed 29.7 million square feet of office space over four quarters, with year-to-date absorption of 16.7 million square feet putting 2026 on track to end the six-year tenant contraction. Canadian net absorption totals 4.4 million square feet YTD and is tracking to exceed 2019 levels. However, performance is uneven: NYC, Dallas, Austin, Houston, San Francisco, and San Jose are surging, while Los Angeles, Chicago, St. Louis, and Washington, D.C., remain unstable.
stories.impact: Office recovery signals marginal improvement in urban office-anchored multifamily demand in top-tier markets (NYC, Austin, SF Bay), supporting higher rents and occupancy in downtown and near-CBD submarkets. However, weakness in L.A., Chicago, and D.C. suggests tenant flight from these metros continues; multifamily developers should expect slower-than-historical demand in secondary markets with weak office recovery, particularly D.C. office-reliant suburbs. Office conversions to residential may accelerate in weak-office metros but remain economically challenged.
